title: GenAI / Agentic AI Security Incident
description: Schema for a single incident entry in the genai_incidents dataset, a consolidated index of GenAI and agentic AI security incidents. Every entry is mapped to four core taxonomies (OWASP LLM Top 10, OWASP Agentic (ASI) Top 10, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS) where applicable, plus optional companion MAESTRO and experimental VERIS crosswalk fields.

source_ids.description: Upstream identifiers when consolidated from external sources (e.g. AIID-123, CVE-2025-xxxxx, ATLAS-AML.CS0001, AVID-2024-V005)

cwe_ids.description: Common Weakness Enumeration identifiers (e.g. CWE-79, CWE-918).

capec_ids.description: MITRE CAPEC attack-pattern identifiers, derived from the entry's CWEs via the authoritative CWE->CAPEC map (mappings/cwe_capec.json). A complete (uncapped) denormalisation — see DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

purl.description: Package-URLs (purl, pkg:type/namespace/name) derived from structured GHSA/OSV `affected` identifiers — entity-resolution anchors for affected packages. See DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

exploited_in_wild.description: True when one of the entry's CVEs appears in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

kev_date_added.description: Earliest date the entry's CVE(s) were added to the CISA KEV catalog.

aiid_id.description: Canonical AI Incident Database numeric ID where this entry has an AIID counterpart.

disclosure_date.description: Public disclosure date when distinct from the incident date.

date.description: ISO date, year-only, or year-month allowed

description.description: Free text aggregated verbatim from upstream advisories. UNTRUSTED: may contain raw HTML / exploit payloads (e.g. '') from the original write-ups. Consumers MUST escape/sanitize before rendering it as HTML or Markdown.

description_provenance.description: Provenance of the current description field's content. verbatim = copied unmodified from an upstream source. summary = model-assisted paraphrase of upstream prose, pre-generated offline and committed under data/summaries/, never generated during make build. original = independently composed from facts/metadata, not a paraphrase of any single upstream source's prose. Absence means not yet assessed.

description_source.description: Short slug naming which upstream ingest contributed the CURRENT description field's content (e.g. aiaaic), meaningful only when description_provenance is set. Needed because description (and this field) are set once by whichever entry survives dedup as the merge target and are never overwritten by later merges, unlike source_ids and tags which merge/union across every absorbed duplicate.

content_license.description: Row-level license-obligation marker: this entry's CONTENT derives from an upstream source whose license imposes obligations (attribution, possibly share-alike) on the row itself, over and above the repository's own LICENSE-DATA. Source-generic by design — the source is named in the `source` VALUE, never in the field name, so any future source with row-level obligations reuses this mechanism unchanged. Set at ingest, in lockstep with description_source, by whichever entry survives dedup as the merge target; like description_source it is EXCLUDED from merge_into's union/absorb behaviour (that exclusion is what keeps it sticky and truthful) and is never overwritten by a later merge. Surfaces: data/incidents.json and the HuggingFace export carry it in full; data/incidents.min.json carries it on marked rows only, absent elsewhere; the STIX bundle mirrors it per-row as an `x_content_license` custom property (D14) — emitted from this field once the WS0-T3 Phase B rebuild populates it, and until then from an interim AIAAIC-source heuristic that is retired at that rebuild; MISP carries no description at all and so no marker (D12(b), as revised by D14). Absence means no row-level obligation is known for this entry — NOT that the entry is unencumbered.

source.description: Slug of the upstream source imposing the obligation, drawn from the same vocabulary as description_source (e.g. aiaaic). The obligation is source-specific; the mechanism is not.

license.description: SPDX license identifier of the upstream content license, e.g. CC-BY-SA-4.0.

license_url.description: Canonical URL of the license deed or legal code. Supply it wherever the license has a stable public URL: a consumer holding only incidents.min.json may see no other license surface.

attribution.description: Human-readable attribution target — the party to credit under the license's attribution clause, e.g. 'AIAAIC Repository'.

attribution_url.description: URL to credit alongside attribution. Optional: not every source publishes a stable one.

obligations.description: Which obligations actually attach to this row, stated explicitly rather than inferred from `license`, so that a later waiver or narrowing by the source downgrades a VALUE (drop 'share-alike') instead of changing the field's shape.

attack_vector.description: Primary attack mechanism — free-form but should match one of the controlled values where possible.

affected.description: Vendor, product, organization, or system affected

reversibility_class.description: Reversibility of the action that closed the incident (#74), ordered least→most severe: read-only = no state mutation; reversible = undoable in-session or by trivial in-system action; external-reversible = undoable only via an external compensating action (refund, retraction, cleanup); irreversible = no compensating action possible. Landmark-tier only, assigned via data/curation_overrides.json where source evidence describes the closing action. Absent = unassessed, NOT read-only. The enum carries no lexical order — consumers must rank explicitly.

discovery_method.description: How the incident was first surfaced (lineage: VERIS 1.4.1 discovery_method, flattened and AI-adapted; media-report has no VERIS parent). Landmark-tier only, assigned via data/curation_overrides.json where the source states the discovery channel — same evidence-gated mechanism as reversibility_class (#74). Absent = unassessed, NOT internally detected.

quality_tier.description: How well-vetted the entry is. `curated` = hand-written or maintainer-reviewed; `reviewed` = sourced from a maintained research catalogue; `auto` = bulk-ingested.

confidence.description: Transparent, rule-derived confidence in the entry (see DATA_DICTIONARY.md). high = curated/reviewed OR 2+ distinct sources with a CVE; medium = 2+ sources OR has a CVE/CVSS; low = a single auto-tier source.

tier.description: Curated/notable `landmark` incidents vs the comprehensive vulnerability/advisory `feed` (INCLUSION.md §5). landmark = curated, AIID-linked real-world, ai-harm, or real-world-category; feed = the CVE/GHSA/OSV bulk. Cite the landmark count for headlines.

source_count.description: Number of distinct upstream sources (source_ids) corroborating the entry.

source_status.description: Whether the entry is still emitted by at least one source on the latest build (`active`) or was retained from a prior build after all its sources dropped it (`retained`).

first_seen.description: Date the entry first entered the dataset (provenance alias of `added`).

last_seen.description: Date the entry's content was last confirmed/updated from a source (provenance alias of `updated`).

corpus.description: Which sub-corpus the entry belongs to. `security` = exploitation, vulnerability, misuse; `ai-harm` = bias/discrimination/social harm without a security primitive.

owasp_llm.description: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) codes

owasp_dsgai.description: OWASP Data Security for GenAI codes (legacy/companion)

added.description: Date this entry was first added to the dataset

allOf.$comment: Row-level license obligations are per-source. Today only AIAAIC-origin descriptions carry one, so every entry whose description_source is aiaaic must also carry content_license. When another source acquires row-level obligations, extend this conditional per source — re-scope it, never drop it.
